title_en: Jiangsu Bairuite Trading Co., Ltd. v. Zhang Yuehong — dispute over unjust enrichment
ruling_gist_en: Where an infringer, after performing its payment obligations under a settlement agreement reached during enforcement, requests the victim's close relatives to refund nursing care fees for unexpired years on the ground of unjust enrichment because the victim died prematurely, such a claim shall not be upheld.

full_text_en:
Jiangsu Bairuite Trading Co., Ltd. v. Zhang Yuehong — dispute over unjust enrichment

【Ruling Summary】

Where a tortfeasor has performed its payment obligations under an enforcement settlement agreement, and subsequently, due to the victim's premature death, seeks the return of nursing expenses for unexpired expected years from the victim's close relatives on the ground of unjust enrichment, such claim shall not be supported.

Plaintiff: Jiangsu Bairuite Trading Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 3, Fangang South Road, Dongtai City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal representative: Chen Meifang, Chairwoman of the Company.

Defendant: Zhang Yuehong, female, 31 years old, Han nationality, residing in Dongtai City, Jiangsu Province.

Plaintiff Jiangsu Bairuite Trading Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Bairuite Company) filed a lawsuit with the Dongtai People's Court of Jiangsu Province against Defendant Zhang Yuehong regarding a dispute over unjust enrichment.

Plaintiff Bairuite Company alleged: Defendant Zhang Yuehong is the daughter of Zhang Longxi, and after Zhang Longxi was injured, she acted as his legal representative. In July 2013, Zhang Longxi filed a lawsuit with the Dongtai People's Court for a dispute over liability for damages suffered by a service provider, requesting Zhou Dongxiang and Bairuite Company to jointly compensate RMB 898,942.18. During the trial, Bairuite Company objected to Zhang Longxi's claim for 20 years of nursing expenses, arguing that such expenses had not yet been incurred and that it would be appropriate to support only 5 years, with the possibility of further claims if nursing was still needed after 5 years. After trial, the Dongtai Court determined that Zhang Longxi's total losses were RMB 1,147,662.85 (including 20 years of nursing expenses of RMB 867,320), and ordered the plaintiff in this case to bear 30% of the liability for compensation, i.e., RMB 359,298 (including 30% of the 20-year nursing expenses of RMB 260,196, and solatium of RMB 15,000). During enforcement, the parties reached a settlement agreement, and the plaintiff in this case paid compensation totaling RMB 300,000, which was remitted to the defendant's bank card. Zhang Longxi died on November 22, 2014, and no longer required nursing care. The actual nursing period was only 906 days, less than 2.5 years. Calculated based on 5 years of nursing expenses, the plaintiff in this case should only pay RMB 65,049. As the daughter and former legal representative of Zhang Longxi, the defendant accepted the compensation, and the caregiver should return the unused portion of the nursing expenses of RMB 132,012 to the plaintiff. Therefore, the plaintiff filed this lawsuit, requesting: (1) the defendant to return RMB 132,012 as unjust enrichment; (2) the litigation costs to be borne by the defendant.

Defendant Zhang Yuehong argued: (1) Zhang Yuehong is not a proper defendant in this case. Zhang Yuehong's acceptance of the compensation was an agency act. The agency act was confirmed by the court during the trial and enforcement proceedings, and the compensation paid had been used to repay Zhang Longxi's debts, cover subsequent treatment and nursing care, etc. (2) The plaintiff Bairuite Company's payment of compensation was an act of performing its obligations determined by a legally effective court judgment. The plaintiff's request for the return of the compensation paid lacks legal basis. (3) The settlement agreement reached by the parties was a re-disposition of their own rights. Once the settlement agreement is fully performed, neither party may repudiate it. In summary, the defendant requests the court to reject the plaintiff's claims in accordance with the law.

The Dongtai People's Court found the following facts at first instance:

At about 2:00 p.m. on May 30, 2012, Zhang Longxi and another person were modifying the wall of Room 904, Building 4, Xin Ning Xin Guang Apartment, No. 3, Jin Hai Zhong Road, owned by the plaintiff Bairuite Company. While chiseling the wall on the east side of the south balcony of Room 904, Zhang Longxi accidentally fell from the louver window on the ninth floor south balcony to the ground and was injured.

On May 30, 2013, a forensic medical examination of Zhang Longxi's injuries concluded that Zhang Longxi's craniocerebral injury resulting in a vegetative state constituted Grade I disability for personal injury. Zhang Longxi had completely lost the ability to work, required long-term nursing care, and needed two caregivers. On July 18, 2013, Zhang Longxi filed a lawsuit with the court requesting the employer Zhou Dongxiang and the property owner Bairuite Company to compensate for various losses arising from the accident. His daughter Zhang Yuehong acted as his legal representative in the proceedings. On September 9, 2013, the court entered a civil judgment (2013) Dong Min Chu Zi No. 0901, holding that the losses from the accident should be apportioned among Zhou Dongxiang, Bairuite Company, and Zhang Longxi at 45%, 30%, and 25% respectively. Based on the forensic medical examination report, because Zhang Longxi's disability prevented him from recovering his ability to care for himself, the nursing period was determined at 20 years considering his age, health status, and other factors, and nursing expenses were assessed at RMB 867,320 (20 years × RMB 21,683/year × 2 persons). Zhang Longxi's total economic losses aggregated RMB 1,147,662.85 (excluding solatium), of which Bairuite Company was to bear 30% of the liability for compensation, i.e., RMB 344,298, plus RMB 15,000 in solatium, and litigation costs of RMB 3,836. Zhou Dongxiang was to compensate RMB 538,948 in losses. The judgment became legally effective.

In November 2013, Zhang Longxi applied for compulsory enforcement of the case. Bairuite Company paid RMB 100,000 from January 2014 to March 2014. On March 24, 2014, Bairuite Company and Zhang Longxi (with Zhang Yuehong as legal representative) entered into an enforcement settlement agreement: Bairuite Company owed Zhang Longxi compensation of RMB 368,333, of which RMB 100,000 had been paid. Bairuite Company was to pay RMB 100,000 each on April 5, 2014, and May 15, 2014. If the full amount was paid on time, Zhang Longxi would waive the remaining balance, and the enforcement of the case would be concluded. The enforcement payment was to be remitted to Zhang Yuehong's bank card. If Bairuite Company failed to perform on time, the original judgment would be restored. Thereafter, Bairuite Company paid RMB 200,000 on time. On November 22, 2014, Zhang Longxi died.

The Dongtai People's Court held at first instance:

This case involves a dispute over unjust enrichment. The issue in dispute is whether the defendant Zhang Yuehong's receipt of the enforcement payment made by the plaintiff Bairuite Company constitutes unjust enrichment, and whether Zhang Yuehong should return the nursing expenses for the unexpired expected years.

Article 236, paragraph 1, of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides that a party must perform a legally effective civil judgment or ruling. A legally effective civil judgment is binding on the parties, and the obligee has the right to demand the obligor to perform its obligations in accordance with the effective civil judgment. In this case, after the civil judgment (2013) Dong Min Chu Zi No. 0901 became legally effective, the plaintiff Bairuite Company was required to perform its compensation obligations as determined in the judgment. The enforcement settlement agreement voluntarily reached between Bairuite Company and Zhang Longxi in March 2014, under which Bairuite Company would pay RMB 300,000 and Zhang Longxi would waive the remaining balance of the RMB 368,333 in compensation, was a disposition of the parties' own rights and could not be changed or revoked without statutory cause. After Bairuite Company performed its obligations under the enforcement settlement agreement, the rights and obligations between the parties arising from Zhang Longxi's injury were terminated.

According to the law, a legal representative may directly conduct litigation activities on behalf of a person with no or limited capacity for civil conduct, for the purpose of protecting the interests of such person. The legal representative themselves have no right to benefit from it. Because Zhang Longxi was in a vegetative state due to his craniocerebral injury, defendant Zhang Yuehong participated in the performance of the civil judgment (2013) Dong Min Chu Zi No. 0901 as his legal representative, and the legal consequences should be borne by Zhang Longxi.

Article 92 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China provides that where a person obtains unjust benefits without a legal basis, causing loss to another person, the benefits so obtained shall be returned to the person who suffered the loss. According to this provision, the constituent elements of unjust enrichment are fourfold: one party obtains a benefit, another party suffers a loss, there is a causal relationship between the benefit and the loss, and the benefit is obtained without a legal basis. First, the plaintiff Bairuite Company's obligation to pay Zhang Longxi was based on the obligation determined by the effective civil judgment, and does not constitute a loss to the party whose interests are harmed in the legal relationship of unjust enrichment. Second, from the perspective of the generality and probability of legal provisions, legislators could not have considered the particularities of individual cases when enacting the law. According to Article 21, paragraph 3, of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases of Personal Injury Compensation, the nursing period shall be calculated until the victim recovers the ability to care for himself; if the victim cannot recover the ability to care for himself due to disability, a reasonable nursing period may be determined based on factors such as the victim's age and health status, but the maximum period shall not exceed 20 years. Nursing expenses are future property losses, more reflective of relief for damages after the victim's disability; the nursing period is a legal presumption of the period during which the victim requires nursing care based on the victim's actual condition, which is a comprehensive judgment made by the judge within the scope of discretion based on legal provisions. The value orientation is to protect the rights of the victim, and the victim also bears the risk that nursing expenses may be insufficient. In the civil judgment (2013) Dong Min Chu Zi No. 0901, the court, based on the expert opinion and factors such as the victim's age and health status, determined that Bairuite Company should bear 30% of the liability for 20 years of nursing expenses of Zhang Longxi. This was a reasonable determination of the compensation due for Zhang Longxi's impaired rights and interests, and was in accordance with the law. Neither Zhang Longxi nor the defendant Zhang Yuehong obtained any unjust benefit from the judgment. Finally, during the enforcement of the civil judgment (2013) Dong Min Chu Zi No. 0901, Bairuite Company and Zhang Longxi reached an enforcement settlement agreement. Zhang Longxi's receipt of RMB 300,000 in compensation through Zhang Yuehong was in accordance with the agreement of the parties and had a legal basis. Moreover, Bairuite Company did not fully perform its compensation obligations under the effective judgment. Its claim that Zhang Yuehong had obtained unjust benefits due to Zhang Longxi's premature death lacked a sufficient basis. Therefore, Bairuite Company's claim for Zhang Yuehong to return RMB 132,012 lacked factual and legal basis, and the court did not support it.

In conclusion, the Dongtai People's Court, in accordance with Article 92 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, and Articles 64 and 142 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on November 14, 2016:

The claim of Plaintiff Jiangsu Bairuite Trading Co., Ltd. for Defendant Zhang Yuehong to return RMB 132,012 as unjust enrichment is dismissed.

After the first-instance judgment, neither party appealed, and the judgment has become legally effective.
